column1: # quality: 1 bpp = mean pixel IoU of the composed syllable vs the font's own glyph at that px (1.0 = identical);
# 2 bpp = mean absolute level difference / 3 (0 = identical). 'all' = every syllable the font draws, ks2350 = the KS X 1001 ones,
# freq = weighted by how often each syllable occurs in a corpus of Korean game translations (1.6 M syllables),
# top500 = mean over the 500 most frequent ones.
# Built 2026-10 at up to 12 lead x 12 tail classes, the pieces chosen with usage weights (sqrt(16 + count) for a KS X 1001
# syllable, sqrt(1 + count) otherwise), so common syllables are drawn closest to the font; they need an engine built
# with 12x12 JSET limits (2026-10 or later): an older one rejects them (more than 8 classes) and falls back to the next face.
# Exception: Single Day (SGDAY) and Neo Dunggeunmo Pro (NDGPR) stay the first 8x8 build with equal weights (12x12 and
# weights gained nothing on them, quality 0.998+), so they also load in older engines; their freq/top500 columns are of that build.
# Latin: every face carries its own Latin, rebuilt with the per-glyph dy (SVFN header bytes 17/18, metrics byte 3;
# graphics/hires_text/README.md, "Per-glyph dy"): drawn at the largest size that fits the cell, the bottom of x z v w u on
# latin_baseline_row = the Hangul no-final bottom row - 1, dy only on the descender letters (g j p q y and the like). An engine
# without dy (before 2026-10-16) draws those glyphs dy rows higher; the Hangul are unchanged.
